# onboarding

What a signed-in account must still do before it can create resources, and the payment page that gets it there.

## GET /v1/onboarding

Operation `onboarding_status_view`.

Read this account's own admission and payment state. What it must still do before it can create resources, and whether a payment page can be opened for it right now.

Scoped to the caller's own tenant. A principal with no tenancy -- a fleet operator, an unscoped credential -- gets the same `404` a cross-tenant probe does; this route has no operator reading of someone else's account, by construction.

Carries three booleans and nothing else. See [`OnboardingStatus`] for what it deliberately leaves out and why.

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [OnboardingStatus](schemas.md#onboardingstatus)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)

## POST /v1/onboarding/checkout

Operation `onboarding_checkout_create`.

Open, or resume, this account's payment page. **Create-or-resume, never create-blindly.** A checkout session expires in about an hour while the account holder may act days later, so a second click adopts the session already open rather than starting another. Two live sessions would be two live checkout URLs, each a bearer credential, each able to complete independently -- a double-billing path, not a harmless retry. Repeating this call is therefore safe: it converges on one subscription.

Reachable by an account that may NOT provision. That is the point: a tenant held `Pending` behind a payment requirement has to be able to pay, and the standing gate that refuses it every other write would otherwise refuse it the one action that clears the gate. The exemption is exactly this action on the caller's own tenancy.

`503` when the deployment has no billing provider configured, when the account has no billing contact on file, or when the provider returned a checkout URL that did not validate. `checkout_available` reports the first two ahead of time.

`409` when a payment would not convert the account (it is paid, or held by an operator), or when a payment is already in progress.

Responses:

- `200`: successful operation, `application/json`: [CheckoutLaunch](schemas.md#checkoutlaunch)
- `4XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
- `5XX`: [Error](schemas.md#error)
